purpose: Input for a future isolated blind audit, not evidence that one occurred
instructions: Choose the single best answer for each item. Search official USMLE and U.S. government-authored evidence. Identify second defensible answers, missing assumptions and item-writing defects. Do not inspect author files, repository, previous chats or answer keys. Return item_id, selected_option, reasoning, ambiguities and evidence URLs. A separate orchestrator must enforce isolation; text instructions alone do not enforce it.

question.vignette: A 7-year-old boy has progressively slowed linear growth and proportionate short stature. Evaluation establishes isolated growth hormone deficiency. Sequencing identifies a biallelic variant in a receptor gene. In a research assay using otherwise identical cells, the normal receptor binds growth hormone-releasing hormone, but the patient-derived receptor does not. The hormone preparation activates cells expressing the normal receptor.
question.lead_in: Which normal endocrine interaction is directly disrupted by this receptor defect?

options.A: Growth hormone acting on receptors in hepatocytes
options.B: IGF-1 acting on receptors in growth-plate cells
options.C: Growth hormone-releasing hormone acting on pituitary somatotrophs
options.D: Somatostatin acting on receptors in pituitary somatotrophs
options.E: Thyroid-stimulating hormone acting on thyroid follicular cells

question.vignette: A 3-week-old boy has recurrent episodes of lethargy with laboratory-confirmed hypoglycemia. Insulin secretion remains inappropriately high during these episodes. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in ABCC8. Functional studies show markedly reduced activity of the channel containing the encoded protein.
question.lead_in: Which change most directly links this defect to inappropriate insulin secretion?

options.A: Reduced activity of beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channels
options.B: Reduced phosphorylation of glucose by beta-cell glucokinase
options.C: Persistent opening of beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channels
options.D: Reduced binding of insulin to receptors on skeletal muscle cells
options.E: Reduced sensitivity of beta cells to a rise in glucose concentration

question.vignette: A 19-year-old woman has mildly elevated fasting glucose documented since childhood, without progressive symptoms. Her father has a similar pattern. Testing identifies a heterozygous loss-of-function variant in GCK. A research team studies glucose-stimulated insulin release from beta cells carrying this variant.
question.lead_in: Which abnormality is most directly attributable to the function of the affected protein?

options.A: Reduced transcription of genes regulating beta-cell development
options.B: Failure of a potassium-channel subunit to respond to rising ATP
options.C: Reduced insulin responsiveness of peripheral target tissues
options.D: Accelerated immune-mediated loss of pancreatic beta cells
options.E: Impaired detection of increasing glucose concentrations by beta cells

question.vignette: A 15-year-old girl has severe obesity and persistent hunger beginning in infancy. In a research study, her circulating leptin activates a normal leptin-receptor reporter system. Cells engineered to express her receptor have normal receptor abundance at the surface and normal leptin binding, but little intracellular signaling after leptin exposure. Otherwise identical cells expressing the normal receptor signal appropriately.
question.lead_in: Which defect best explains these results?

options.A: Reduced synthesis of leptin in adipocytes
options.B: Impaired coupling of the leptin receptor to intracellular signaling
options.C: Reduced affinity of the leptin receptor for its ligand
options.D: Accelerated removal of leptin from the circulation
options.E: Impaired secretion of leptin from adipocytes

question.vignette: A 24-year-old woman is evaluated for infertility. She had normal breast and pubic-hair development but has had infrequent menstrual periods since late adolescence. Evaluation shows anovulation. Her 46,XY sibling has female external genitalia, undescended testes, and markedly underdeveloped Leydig cells. Sequencing finds the same biallelic loss-of-function receptor variant in both siblings.
question.lead_in: Failure to respond to which pair of hormones most directly explains the shared receptor defect?

options.D: Luteinizing hormone and human chorionic gonadotropin
options.E: Growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1
